cases.oracle: Private passwd/group rows and independently specified Linux credential transitions. An independent Python control performs the same real kernel credential calls and proves selected EPERM/readback faults plus invalid purpose, token and replay rejection in the test double. SU and the target report actual IDs, groups, saved IDs, environment and working directory. Authorization device and token replies are modeled and establish no production authority semantics.
cases.comparison: Record the exact ordered setgroups/setresgid/setresuid/getresuid/getresgid calls, live kernel credential snapshots after continued ID reads and mismatched saved-ID fault controls, kernel /proc snapshots, target-exec argv/environment/cwd and target self-report. Every selected fault must prevent target execution and leave the calling shell unchanged. The original no-partial-credential-change wording is evaluated literally in the owned child too; prior real changes in a child that exits are reported as FAIL, not relabeled as rollback. Fault verdicts require the exact call prefix, one selected fault, no containment denial or attempted target exec, and the real actor identity at its observed nonzero exit. Deliberately incorrect native controls must fail this verdict.
cases.purpose: Resolve the selected private account and perform real kernel credential changes with member group/login configuration.
cases.stdout: su-native member real-ids=yes real-groups=yes saved-ids=yes account=yes caller-unchanged=yes
